questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

The radio data shows neither evidence for ongoing jet activity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**neither evidence for**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the error lies in the part "neither evidence for."
 
• **The use of the conjunction "neither" is inappropriate.**
 
• **Neither allows us to make a negative statement about two people or things at the same time.**
 
 
• **But no two things are mentioned in the given statement. Thus, the use of "neither" is incorrect.**
 
 
 
• The correct word to use is "no" before the noun.
 
• The correct statement will be:
 
 
• The radio data shows no evidence for ongoing jet activity. 
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 2**.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

• **The correct verb to use in this sentence is "were" instead of "was" because it is in the subjunctive mood.**
 
• Subjunctive mood is used to express hypothetical or unreal situations.
 
• In this case, the speaker is not actually a clown so the subjunctive mood should be used.
 
• The correct sentence would be:
 
 
• "If I were a clown, I would have made everyone smile." 
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 3**.

questions.question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

The new government's domestic policies could easily __undermine__ the main foreign policy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Enhance**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Antonym means a word that means the opposite of another word.
 
• Let us understand the meaning of the given and the marked words:
 
• The underlined word is **"undermine", which means to weaken or sabotage.**(कमजोर)
 
 
• Example: This could undermine years of hard work.
 
 
 
• **"Enhance" means ****to improve or strengthen something.**(बढ़ाना)
 
 
• ​Example: The drugs will enhance his quality of life.
 
 
 
• ​Thus, the word "enhance" is the antonym of the word "undermine."

​Hence, **the correct answer is option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1, Cripple, is a synonym of undermine and means to disable or cripple something. (अपंग)
 
• Option 2, Weaken, is also a synonym of undermine and means to make something weaker.(कमजोर)
 
• Option 3, Spoil, is not an antonym of undermine and means to damage or ruin something.(खराब करना)

The pudding fell _______ floor with a heart-stopping crash.

• The verb "fell" requires a preposition to indicate where the pudding fell.
 
• The correct preposition in this context is "to", indicating movement towards a destination.
 
• **We can use 'to' as a preposition to indicate a destination or direction**.
 
 
• Example: The cat ran to us as soon as we arrived.
 
 
 
• **In case of the given sentence, the direction in which the pudding fell is discussed.**
 
• Thus, the correct phrase to use is "to the."

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4**.

• "Upon" (Option 1) is also a possible preposition, but it is more formal and less commonly used in everyday speech.
 
• "Up to" (Option 2) suggests proximity or reaching a limit, but it does not convey the idea of falling onto a surface.
 
• "Into the" (Option 3) suggests movement inside something, which is not appropriate in this context.
